solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Lark about with half-hearted nobleman (5)

indicatorNotes.half-hearted: Something half-hearted has lost half its heart, and PEER's heart is the pair EE, so one E goes.

blocks.note: PEER with one of its two central Es removed

annotation.surface: A lord who can only half commit to a bit of fun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lark' could be the bird, but the clue has no birds in it; here it is a spree.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a lark and a caper are both a carefree prank or escapade.

entries.clue: Secures shellfish I meant to add (6)

blocks.note: a postscript is what you write when you meant to add something

annotation.surface: A cook remembering the clams they forgot to put in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I meant to add' is the voice of a letter-writer's afterthought, the classic postscript.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to clamp a thing is to fix it firmly in place, to secure it.

entries.clue: Best, by far, way to add colour? (3,2,3,5)

blocks.note: read literally: putting in a shade, a tint

annotation.surface: A decorator's tip on the finest way to colour something in.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic, hence the question mark: 'shade' as a tint of colour, not as shadow.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to put someone in the shade is to outshine them; literally, a painter puts a shade into a picture.

entries.clue: Sticky thing, dealing with crime (5)

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong, a crime

annotation.surface: A sticky situation that involves some crime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sticky thing' sounds like a tricky situation, but it is a literal gum.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: resin is the gummy substance that oozes from trees.

entries.clue: Full coverage of planet circling towards moon (10)

indicatorNotes.circling: A planet circling something goes all the way round it, so SATURN wraps the other pieces.

annotation.surface: An astronomer's report on a planet swinging round to face a moon.
annotation.walkthrough: IO is crosswordland's favourite moon, and Saturn's rings make 'circling' feel natural.
annotation.definitionFit: Sense of the phrase: saturation coverage leaves nothing untouched, full coverage.

entries.clue: Chewed up list pet drops from mouth (7)

indicatorNotes.Chewed up: Something chewed up is mashed out of its original shape, so the letters lose their order.

annotation.surface: A dog has chewed up the list and dropped the soggy bits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drops' looks like a verb for the pet letting go; it is a plural noun, drops of saliva.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: spittle is saliva, the drops that fall from a mouth.

entries.clue: Furiously sound horn to help arrest (5,3,4)

blocks.note: to nail a suspect is to catch them

annotation.surface: A driver leaning angrily on the horn to summon help with an arrest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Furiously' looks like an adverb for the horn-blowing, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to fight tooth and nail is to fight with every weapon, furiously.

entries.clue: Top up her grace, getting smashed (8)

indicatorNotes.getting smashed: Something smashed is broken into bits that can be put back in any order.

annotation.surface: A duchess keeps having her glass refilled until she is drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top up' and 'smashed' conspire to suggest drinks; the definition works just as well for a battery.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to recharge a battery, or a glass, is to top it up.

entries.clue: Highlight missing the first strand of hair (5)

indicatorNotes.missing the first: A word missing its first letter has lost its opening S.

blocks.note: to highlight a point is to stress it
drop the S at the front

annotation.surface: A hairdresser has missed the first strand when doing highlights.
annotation.walkthrough: Highlights are a salon treatment, so 'Highlight' looks like part of the hair scene; here it means emphasise.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a tress is a lock or strand of hair.

entries.clue: Acting alone? (3-3,4)

blocks.note: the surface reading: doing a deed without accomplices
flags the theatrical reading: performing on stage with no other cast

annotation.surface: Someone doing a deed without help.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Acting alone' is what police say of a lone culprit; read as theatre, it is a solo performance.
annotation.definitionFit: Theatre sense: a show with a single performer is acting alone in the literal sense.

entries.clue: Help fool start to succeed in Congress (6)

indicatorNotes.start to: The start of a word is its first letter, so 'start to succeed' is S.
indicatorNotes.in: Being in something means sitting inside it, so S goes inside IT.

annotation.surface: A plea for a clown to help get things going in the US Congress.
annotation.walkthrough: Congress with a capital C looks like the US legislature; here it is sexual congress, which crosswords call 'it'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to assist someone and to help them are the same act of lending a hand.

entries.clue: Fragrant setting snubbed conference organiser (7)

indicatorNotes.snubbed: A snub nose is cut short, so a snubbed word loses its tip, the last letter.

blocks.note: SCENE, a setting, with its tail cut off
TED, the organisation behind TED Talks conferences

annotation.surface: An organiser who was snubbed at a conference venue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' reads as slighted, but means shortened, as in a snub nose.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something scented has a perfume, so it is fragrant.

entries.clue: Italian side brought over English official to meddle (9)

indicatorNotes.brought over: Bringing something over turns it upside down, which in a down clue reverses E REF.

blocks.note: Inter Milan, the Italian football club
a ref, referee, is a match official

annotation.surface: An Italian football club flew in an English referee, accused of meddling.
annotation.walkthrough: Inter Milan is a football club, which makes the referee part of the same story.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to interfere is to meddle in others' affairs.

entries.clue: Attention-grabbing sound in extremely trite melody (5)

indicatorNotes.in: Being in something means sitting inside it, so HEM goes inside.
indicatorNotes.extremely: The extremes of a word are its two ends, so 'extremely trite' is T and E.

blocks.note: the outer letters of trite, split T...E

annotation.surface: A critic hears an eye-catching sound buried in a hackneyed tune.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'hem' is the throat-clearing noise made to catch someone's attention.
annotation.definitionFit: Music sense: a theme is the main tune of a piece, its melody.

entries.clue: Arrogance of attitude worn by troublemakers more nakedly (4-10)

indicatorNotes.worn by: A garment worn by someone goes around them, so the attitude wraps the troublemakers.
indicatorNotes.nakedly: Stripped naked, a word loses its outer layer, so 'more' becomes OR.

blocks.note: a stance is an attitude; split S...TANCE
an ELF and an IMP, two mischievous sprites

annotation.surface: A pompous attitude is on display from troublemakers who flaunt ever more flesh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Troublemakers' is plural for a reason: it supplies two mischievous sprites, not one.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: self-importance is an inflated sense of one's own worth, arrogance.

entries.clue: Very high key’s what ends Callas, if you ask me (9)

indicatorNotes.ends: What ends a word is its last letter, here the S of Callas.

blocks.note: the Alt key on a keyboard
IMO, internet shorthand for in my opinion

annotation.surface: A critic's view that Maria Callas finishes on a stratospheric note.
annotation.walkthrough: The key is a computer key, not a musical one, despite the soprano Maria Callas in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Italian music term: altissimo, literally 'highest', names the very top register.

entries.clue: Mass decree getting disorderly fellows the booze (5,2,6)

indicatorNotes.getting disorderly: Getting disorderly means falling out of order, so the letters of M and DECREE are jumbled.

blocks.note: taken as written, then shuffled with the M

annotation.surface: An order that rowdy blokes are to be given drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like a church service beside 'decree', but it is the physics M; 'the' is wordplay, not part of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: crème de menthe is a mint liqueur, one kind of booze.

entries.clue: Strain to bite around seed in salad (4,3)

indicatorNotes.around: Turned around means facing the other way, so TUNE NIP is read backwards.

blocks.note: a strain of music is a tune
a nip is a small bite

annotation.surface: Someone straining to chew a hard seed in their salad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like a verb of effort; it is the musical noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: pine nuts are pine-cone seeds, often scattered in salads.

entries.clue: FC shared a redesigned piece of apparel (9)

indicatorNotes.redesigned: Something redesigned keeps its materials but takes a new shape, so the letters are rearranged.

annotation.surface: A football club released a new version of its kit.
annotation.walkthrough: FC, football club, supplies two awkward consonants; football scarves make the surface ring true.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a headscarf is one item of clothing, a piece of apparel.

entries.clue: Short shirt covers ribs, but not guts? (5)

indicatorNotes.covers: A shirt covers what is under it, so TEE goes round the rest.
indicatorNotes.but not guts: The guts of a word are its insides, so without them 'ribs' is just R and S.

annotation.surface: A cropped top that shows the ribcage but hides the belly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short shirt' reads as a crop top, but 'Short' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Manner sense: a terse reply is short, clipped to the bare minimum.

entries.clue: Trendy doll with rotating arm grasps bits of food (7,7)

indicatorNotes.rotating: Rotating turns something round, so GUN is read backwards.

blocks.note: to get an idea is to grasp it

annotation.surface: A fashionable action figure with a swivelling arm clutches some morsels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arm' suggests the doll's limb; it is a firearm.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: chicken nuggets are small breaded bits of chicken.

entries.clue: One might explain constant abuse of air rifle (9)

indicatorNotes.abuse of: Abusing something means misusing it, twisting its letters out of their proper order.

blocks.note: c, the speed of light, the classic constant

annotation.surface: A warning about constant misuse of an air gun, and someone to explain it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Constant' reads as the adjective 'continual'; it is the physics noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: a clarifier is whatever makes something clear, so one might explain.

entries.clue: Paint two beasts, one consuming second (8)

indicatorNotes.consuming: A beast consuming something has it inside, so the lion swallows the S.

blocks.note: the second beast, a lion, split L...ION

annotation.surface: An instruction to paint two animals, one of them devouring another.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paint' looks like an order to an artist; it is the definition, a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: emulsion is the everyday water-based paint for walls.

entries.clue: Finale turned into large-scale frenzy (7)

indicatorNotes.turned: Something turned round faces the other way, so END is read backwards.
indicatorNotes.into: Going into something means ending up inside it, so the reversed word sits inside MASS.

blocks.note: mass, as in mass production; split MA...SS

annotation.surface: A grand finale that descended into widespread chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large-scale' is an adjective, which is why the word it gives works adjectivally too: mass hysteria, mass market.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: madness and frenzy both mean wild, uncontrolled behaviour.

entries.clue: Darling son, little man, tucking into pastry (10)

indicatorNotes.tucking into: Someone tucking into food has it going inside them, so the man goes inside the pastry.

annotation.surface: A fond parent watches their small boy eating a pie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little man' reads as one affectionate phrase for the boy, but the two words work separately.
annotation.definitionFit: Term of endearment: sweetheart and darling are interchangeable pet names.

entries.clue: Was trumpeter paid to play clubs ultimately well trained? (10)

annotation.definitionNote: as printed; the sense is 'trumpeted', acted as the trumpeter

indicatorNotes.ultimately: Ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter of 'well'.

blocks.note: a pro, professional, is paid to play
a gun trained on a target is aimed

annotation.surface: A musician wonders whether a hired trumpet player who plays clubs is properly schooled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' goes forward to 'well', not back to 'clubs', and 'trained' is about pointing a gun, not schooling.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: to trumpet news is to proclaim it loudly.

entries.clue: Stop rave taking over a university eatery (10)

indicatorNotes.taking over: Taking something over means taking it in, so REST RANT absorbs A and U.

annotation.surface: A party is stopped when it spreads onto a campus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rave' looks like the noun, a party; it is the verb, to rant.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a restaurant is a place to eat, an eatery.

entries.clue: Men request bard changes characteristic of old master (14)

indicatorNotes.changes: Changes here is a verb: the phrase alters, and its letters come out in a new order.

annotation.surface: A group asks Shakespeare to revise his work.
annotation.walkthrough: The bard points at Shakespeare, but the old master is a painter.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective from a name: -esque means 'in the style of', here the Dutch old master Rembrandt.

entries.clue: Car race perhaps contains large predictive software component (12)

indicatorNotes.contains: Something that contains another holds it inside, so COMPETE holds the L.

blocks.note: racing is one way to compete; split COMP...ETE

annotation.surface: A motor race uses a big piece of software to predict the result.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks race as one example of competing; 'Car race' is not one unit.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: autocomplete predicts the rest of what you are typing.

entries.clue: Chopped fish tops a flatbread for each of us (3,6)

indicatorNotes.Chopped: Something chopped has a piece cut off, here the H at the end of PERCH.
indicatorNotes.tops: In a down clue what tops the rest sits above it, so it comes first.

blocks.note: PERCH with its last letter cut off

annotation.surface: A recipe: diced fish on top of a flatbread, one each.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' looks like kitchen prep, but it docks a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin phrase: per capita means 'by heads', so per person, for each of us.

entries.clue: Couple of notes in map book where the ancients sank (8)

indicatorNotes.in: Being in something means sitting inside it, so the two notes go inside the map book.

blocks.note: N = note, plus TI, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A pair of jottings in an atlas marks the site of an old shipwreck.
annotation.walkthrough: The two notes are different kinds: one is the abbreviation for 'note', the other a sol-fa note.
annotation.definitionFit: Legend: Atlantis was the ancient island civilisation that sank beneath the sea.

entries.clue: Animal fur, primarily illegal (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: Primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of illegal.

blocks.note: an animal's fur is its coat

annotation.surface: Trading in this creature's pelt is basically against the law.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Animal fur' reads as one phrase, a pelt; 'Animal' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the coati is a raccoon-like mammal of the Americas.

entries.clue: Juiciest moments involving India’s cricket match? (8)

indicatorNotes.involving: Something involving another takes it in, so MOS wraps round the I.

blocks.note: mos, plural of mo, a moment; split MO...S
I = India in the phonetic alphabet; the 's is just possessive

annotation.surface: The most exciting bits of an India cricket international.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Juiciest' suggests the most exciting moments; it means the wettest.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal sense: the juiciest fruit is the moistest.

entries.clue: The Sun’s feature possibly recalled singers initially selling cannabis (8)

indicatorNotes.recalled: Recalled means called back, so RATS is read from the back.
indicatorNotes.initially: Initially means at the start, so take the first letter of selling.

blocks.note: informers who 'sing' to the police are rats

annotation.surface: A tabloid story: pop singers remembered dealing drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, which makes the surface a showbiz scandal; the definition means the star itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a sunspot is the Sun's version of a starspot, hence 'possibly'.

entries.clue: Quality anime ruined with insertion of clear British line (5,8)

indicatorNotes.ruined: Something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so ANIME's letters are scrambled.
indicatorNotes.with insertion of: Insertion puts extra material in, so RID joins the letters being scrambled.

blocks.note: to clear a place of pests is to rid it

annotation.surface: A review of high-grade Japanese animation spoilt by an added British scene.
annotation.walkthrough: The prime meridian, 0° longitude, runs through Greenwich in London, which makes it a British line.
annotation.definitionFit: Geography: the line of zero longitude is drawn through Greenwich, England.

entries.clue: Always the learner, filling head still (12)

indicatorNotes.filling: A filling sits inside something, so the first pieces go inside the head.

blocks.note: a ness is a headland; split N...ESS

annotation.surface: A forever-student whose head is still being filled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' is geography, a headland as in Loch Ness or Sheerness, not the thing on your shoulders.
annotation.definitionFit: Adverb sense: 'still' as in 'still, we tried' means nevertheless, even so.

entries.clue: Workshops had inventions eclipsing Rubik’s foremost (8)

indicatorNotes.eclipsing: Something eclipsing another covers it, so LIES goes round the R.
indicatorNotes.foremost: Foremost means at the front, so take the first letter of Rubik's.

annotation.surface: Workshops produced inventions that outshone the Rubik's cube.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inventions' suggests gadgets, which fits the Rubik's cube, but here they are fibs.
annotation.definitionFit: French loanword: an atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a workshop.

entries.clue: Chief of ancillary staff constrained by refusal of French Emperor (8)

indicatorNotes.Chief of: The chief of a group is at its head, so take the first letter of ancillary.
indicatorNotes.constrained by: Something constrained by another is held in by it, so NON goes round the rest.

annotation.surface: The head of support staff held back by a French emperor's refusal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French Emperor' seems one phrase; 'of French' belongs to the refusal and 'Emperor' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Napoleon Bonaparte is the best-known Emperor of the French.

entries.clue: Last ingredient in kebab I’d expect (5)

indicatorNotes.ingredient in: An ingredient is part of a mixture, so the answer is a part of the words that follow.

blocks.note: runs from the end of kebab into expect

annotation.surface: Someone predicting what goes into a kebab last.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last ingredient' reads as one phrase; 'Last' is a verb, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to last is to endure, and abide has that old sense of enduring.

entries.clue: Voters go for post-inaugural address (10)

indicatorNotes.post-inaugural: Post means after and inaugural means first, so keep what comes after the first letter.

blocks.note: SELECT (go for) without its first letter
to address a crowd is to orate

annotation.surface: Voters pick the speech made after a president takes office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Post-inaugural address' reads as a presidential speech; split the phrase, and 'post-inaugural' acts on the word before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Collective noun: the electorate is the whole body of voters.

entries.clue: Wrongly interpret film before Kurosawa picture’s delayed (12)

annotation.surface: A subtitler garbles a film because a Kurosawa release is late.
annotation.walkthrough: The first 'film' is a thin layer, not a movie; the Kurosawa picture is the movie.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain sense: to mistranslate is to interpret words wrongly from another language.

entries.clue: Crew captivated by bottle of retro-futurist design (9)

indicatorNotes.captivated by: Captivated means held captive, so the crew is locked inside the bottle.

annotation.surface: Sailors charmed by a bottle of something with a vintage sci-fi look.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve or courage.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: steampunk pairs Victorian steam machinery with futuristic invention.

entries.clue: Singing coach engineers small opening for useless tenor finally (10)

indicatorNotes.opening for: The opening of a word is its first letter, U for useless.
indicatorNotes.finally: Finally means at the end, so take the last letter of tenor.

annotation.surface: A vocal coach builds a small way in for a hopeless tenor.
annotation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army; 'opening' looks like a gap the engineers build.
annotation.definitionFit: Opera sense: a répétiteur rehearses singers in their parts, a singing coach.

entries.clue: Supporters drinking beer back to coarse language at bar? (8)

indicatorNotes.drinking: Something drinking takes liquid in, so LEGS takes in ALE.
indicatorNotes.back to: The back of a word is its last letter, E for coarse.

annotation.surface: Football fans drinking in the pub turn to bad language.
annotation.walkthrough: The bar is the legal profession, not a pub; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Barristers are 'called to the bar', and their jargon is legalese.

entries.clue: Nuisance to pursue river with most bass (7)

indicatorNotes.to pursue: To pursue is to come after, so PEST follows DEE.

blocks.note: the Dee, a river in Britain

annotation.surface: An annoying angler chasing the river with the most sea bass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bass' suggests fish in a river; it is low pitch.
annotation.definitionFit: Sound sense: the deepest voice is the one lowest in pitch, with most bass.

entries.clue: Unopened fruit’s stolen here, we hear (7)

indicatorNotes.Unopened: Something unopened has not had its front removed; here the fruit loses its opening letter.

annotation.surface: Rumour has it that the unpeeled fruit has been nicked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'We hear' looks like the usual signal of a sound-alike; here it is part of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic gloss: earshot is the range within which we hear, so 'here, we hear'.

entries.clue: Respect, alas, yet to be remastered for this technology? (8,6)

indicatorNotes.to be remastered: A remastered recording is reworked from the original, so the letters are reworked into a new order.

annotation.surface: Fans lament that some old recordings still await remastering for tape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Remastered' fits the music surface and the old technology at once.
annotation.definitionFit: Pointer definition: 'this technology' is whatever plays remastered tapes, the cassette player.

entries.clue: Appropriate to buy piece of meat when abandoning hunt? (7)

indicatorNotes.when abandoning: Abandoning something leaves it behind, so CHASE is dropped from PURCHASE.

blocks.note: a hunt is a chase; this is removed, leaving PUR

annotation.surface: Is it right to buy your meat rather than hunting it?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as the adjective 'fitting'; it is the verb, to take.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to appropriate something is to take it for yourself, to purloin it.

entries.clue: Suffer supporting live act (6)

indicatorNotes.supporting: A support holds from below, so in a down clue this piece comes second.

blocks.note: to be is to live, exist
to have a cold is to suffer from it

annotation.surface: A performer toils to back a live show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Live act' reads as a gig; 'live' is a verb, and 'act' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to behave is to act or conduct oneself.

entries.clue: Iron spirit set back bone (5)

indicatorNotes.set back: Set back means put backwards, so RUM is reversed.

blocks.note: Fe, the chemical symbol for iron

annotation.surface: A strong drink knocks someone back and hurts a bone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set back' suggests an injury; it is an instruction for direction.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the femur is the thigh bone.

entries.clue: Joined force, displaying prior employment (5)

annotation.surface: Someone enlisted, showing their previous job history.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joined force' reads as enlisted in the police; 'force' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: fused means joined into one.

entries.clue: Rocket has spoiled dessert (9)

indicatorNotes.spoiled: Something spoiled is ruined, so the letters no longer stand in good order.

annotation.surface: Salad leaves have ruined the pudding.
annotation.walkthrough: Rocket is a salad leaf (arugula), which keeps the surface in the kitchen.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: strawberry shortcake is a classic dessert.

entries.clue: Adjust whiskey cased in wood (5)

indicatorNotes.cased in: Something cased in a material is enclosed by it, so the wood goes round W.

blocks.note: W = whiskey in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A distiller changes how whiskey is aged in wooden casks.
annotation.walkthrough: Whiskey really is aged in wooden casks, so the surface is a distillery; here it is just a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to tweak is to make a small adjustment.

entries.clue: Polish article in Die Welt reflects colourful phenomenon in the main (3,4)

indicatorNotes.reflects: A reflection is a mirror image, so the combined letters read backwards.

blocks.note: to polish a text is to edit it

annotation.surface: A Polish piece in a German newspaper reports on something colourful at sea.
annotation.walkthrough: Die Welt is a German newspaper, which makes 'Polish' look like a nationality and 'article' like a report.
annotation.definitionFit: 'The main' is old poetic English for the sea, where an algal bloom turns the water red.

entries.clue: Fancy sheets daughter’s set on (5)

indicatorNotes.set on: Set on means placed on top, which in a down clue puts D first.

blocks.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper

annotation.surface: A daughter has her heart set on smart bedlinen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy sheets' reads as posh bedding; 'Fancy' is the definition, and the sheets are paper.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to fancy something is to dream of it, to imagine it.

entries.clue: Fix us sautéed nosh of African provenance (5,8)

indicatorNotes.Fix: To fix something is to sort it out, so the letters are sorted into a new order.

annotation.surface: A request for a pan-fried dish from Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nosh' is British slang for food, and 'Fix' reads as 'make for us'.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective of origin: something South Sudanese comes from South Sudan in Africa.

entries.clue: In middle of gardening drunk, plant mysterious things (9)

indicatorNotes.In middle of: The middle of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter, here E.

blocks.note: the fifth of gardening's nine letters

annotation.surface: A drunk in mid-gardening plants something odd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb for the gardener; it is a noun, the heather genus.
annotation.definitionFit: Plural noun: esoterica are obscure matters known only to a few, mysterious things.

entries.clue: Going through facts, knock out American language (6)

indicatorNotes.Going through: Something going through another passes into its middle, so KO sits inside the facts.

annotation.surface: A researcher sifts the facts to eliminate an American dialect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American' means Native American here: the language of the Sioux of the northern plains.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Dakota is one of the Sioux languages of North America.

entries.clue: High time for a holiday? (4,6)

blocks.note: the surface reading: the idiom for 'about time'; read literally, the top time
the busiest part of the holiday year

annotation.surface: Someone decides it is well past time to get away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High time' is the idiom for 'about time'; read literally it is the top of the season.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal reading: the peak is the highest point, so the peak season is the high time for holidays.

entries.clue: Chop tail off vermin with rodents about (5)

indicatorNotes.tail off: The tail of a word is its last letter, N for vermin.
indicatorNotes.about: About means around, so MICE surround the N.

annotation.surface: An instruction to cut the tail off a rat with mice running around.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chop tail off' reads as one gruesome order, but 'Chop' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Kitchen sense: to mince meat is to chop it very finely.
